Municipality
              of
     Anchorage


     P.O Box 390                  GIRDWOOD VALLEY SERVICE AREA BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
      Girdwood, Alaska 99587                         Mike Edgington & Jennifer Wingard, Co-Chairs
      http://www.muni.org/gbos                           Briana Sullivan, Brian Burnett, Kellie Okonek
    Suzanne LaFrance, Mayor
                            January 26 2026
                     GBOS Regular Meeting
                              Minutes Final
         7:00 p.m. via Microsoft Teams & Girdwood Community Room

This hybrid meeting is taking place via Microsoft Teams & at the Girdwood Community Room, 250 Egloff Rd:

The Girdwood Board of Supervisors is subject to the Alaska Open Meetings Act as found in Alaska Statute 44.62.310
and Anchorage Municipal Code1.25 - Public Meetings.
The Girdwood Board of Supervisors operates under the Girdwood Public Meetings Standards of Conduct.

Call to Order 7:02 p.m. Jennifer Wingard, Co-Chair

Land Acknowledgement: The Girdwood Board of Supervisors acknowledges the indigenous peoples of Alaska, whose land we
reside on. The community of Girdwood, situated between the areas known to be Dena'ina and Alutiiq homeland, respects the people
who were stewards of this land for generations. We commit to the continued stewardship of this land and are grateful to be part of a
wider community that seeks to maintain a sustainable use of Girdwood Valley for present and future peoples.

Roll Call & Disclosures.
Attending are Jennifer Wingard (JW), Briana Sullivan (BS), Kellie Okonek (KO), Mike Edgington (ME) arr. 7:05
Brian Burnett is excused.

ME takes chair after roll call is complete.

    •   Announcements:
      CHUGACH ELECTRIC ASSOCIATION scheduled power outage THU Jan 29 12:01AM-4AM

    •   Upcoming meetings:
     GBOS WS re Intergovernmental Charges                   Date TBA
     GBOS Rules & Goals part 2                               Date TBA
     GBOS WS RE: Funding Capital projects via Leaseback Funding Date TBA
    •  GBOS Seats D and E terms end in 2026. Candidate filing for the 2026 Regular Municipal Election will open on
        Friday, January 16, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. and close on Friday, January 30, 2026 at 5:00 p.m.

        Elections Candidate Information

Agenda Revisions and Approval:
January 26 2026 GBOS meeting agenda approved                BS/JW
Amended to add Item #13 in new business                      JW/BS        Assent
Minutes Approval: December 15 GBOS meeting minutes approved  BS/JW        Assent
Consent agenda:    None

       GBOS Meeting Agendas and minutes are available on line: http://www.muni.org/gbos


                                                                                         1

Presentations (10 Min):     Order of presentations, reports and old business item #6 is mixed due to technical
problems during the meeting and availability of presenters. Representation in the minutes matches the original
agenda order.

Chugach Electric Presentation on resuming work on transmission line outside of Girdwood (Julie Hasquet and Mike
Miller, CEA, presenting) See meeting packet for presentation. Upcoming outage on 1/29 with follow up outage
expected Feb 10.

PCZ Case 2026-0042, Amendment to T21C9 to align with the Girdwood Comprehensive Plan related to the rezone of
the old gravel pit to Airport for heli-pad/avalanche mitigation in the Seward Highway Corridor. Scheduled for hearing
MON March 9 at PZC. (Paul Hatcher, Current Planning, presenting). Materials in meeting packet with item #10.

Reports (5 Min):
1.  Legislative Report – Sen. Cathy Giessel, Rep. Ky Holland
Ky Holland reports that session is under way. Working on many different projects/bills.
Assembly members – Z. Johnson/Keith McCormick: Johnson reports that GBOS request for land use authority has
been approved by Assembly. Assembly postponed decision about code change to increase HLBAC to 2 Girdwood
residents. HLB 1 and 5 year plans will be subject of a work session on FRI with vote likely in February. Assembly
considering special levy for ASD funding, which will go to voters in April election. Other tax items have been
postponed indefinitely and will not be included on spring ballot. Property tax assessments, appeal if you think the
assessment is not correct.
Anchorage School Board Liaison – Andy Holleman. No report
HLBAC Report – Tim Charnon. No report.

2.  Supervisor Reports
2026 Officers for all committees. See meeting packet
Sullivan: Fire Dept annual meeting was held. Fire dept is an option for Pick Click Give program
Okonek: Safer Seward Highway public meeting held in January. Comment period extended to end of Febrary.
Discussion with Sean Holland regarding funds for Alyeska Highway traffic calming: repainting sweeps, replacing
bollards, adding flashing You Are Speeding light, extend 30MPH zone farther along Alyeska Highway.
Wingard: MOA GBOS meeting today.

3.  Committee updates to GBOS. None

4.  Standing Reports: See meeting packet
5.  Service Provider Reports (5 mins each): See meeting packet for reports.

PUBLIC COMMENT:
Amanda Tuttle: Property tax assessment increase of 100%+ in the last 2 years. Impact to businesses and
homeowners. Request for GBOS response to MOA.

OLD BUSINESS:
6.  Agenda Item LUC 2512-06: FCC

Motion:
GBOS move to suspend rules and remove ME from chair for the remainder of the meeting.
Motion by JW/2nd KO
3 in favor, 1 opposed (ME) in roll call vote
Motion carries.

Motion:
GBOS moves to assign Jennifer Wingard to serve as chair for the remainder of the meeting.
Motion by KO/JW
4 in favor, 0 opposed
Motion carries.

Point of order: KO states that ME has a conflict of interest related to voting on this matter.
Discussion: Mike states that his interest in FCC is public, not personal, financial or private. He began service on FCC in 2021 as GBOS
co-chair and GBOS LUC supervisor he began attending FCC and became delegate. March/Apr 2021
Jennifer states that the item currently under discussion is if there is a conflict of interest in having a member vote when the outcome of
the vote will determine their role in an outside board and perception of the outside board.
                                                                                         2

JW rules that ME should not vote on the matter to follow, which is re-vote on the GBOS item from November 2025.
With reduced number of GBOS members, chair states that she has researched rules and is able to second motions.

Motion:
GBOS moves to void the Nov 25 vote regarding FCC due to the GBOS failure to uphold the municipal code regarding conflict of
interest.
Motion by KO/JW
Motion carries 3-0
ME is recused from voting on this item

GBOS returns to review the motion voted on at the GBOS November 2025 meeting, below:

   November Motion:
   GBOS moves to adopt the following language from LUC: Whereas there is no evidence of an official appointment or election of an
   FCC delegate from Girdwood since 2020, the Girdwood Land Use Committee agrees that:

     1.  Girdwood does not have a current delegate to the Federation of Community Councils, and
     2.  Girdwood has not had an FCC delegate since January, 2021.

       Group discusses replacing 1 above with: “As of Nov 2025, Girdwood did not have a current delegate to the FCC,” leaving all
         other language from the original motion.

Motion:
GBOS moves to adopt the following language from LUC: Whereas there is no evidence of an official appointment or election of an FCC
delegate from Girdwood since 2020, the Girdwood Land Use Committee agrees that:

              1.  As of Nov 2025, Girdwood did not have a current delegate to the Federation of Community Councils, and
              2.  Girdwood has not had an FCC delegate since January, 2021.

Motion by KO, 2nd JW
Roll call vote 2 in favor, 1 opposed (BS)
Amendment to Motion carries


Motion:
GBOS moves to assign the current LUC supervisor to serve as the FCC delegate.
Motion by KO,2nd JW
Roll call vote 3 in favor, 0 opposed
Motion carries

Discussion about whether a substitute should be designated. This could be taken up by LUC in the future.

Mike Edgington returns from recusal.

Update on FCC Bylaws.
Current draft is in the meeting packet with markup as are the current bylaws, along with links for finding these items on the FCC
website. LUC has not discussed FCC bylaws as they were not published until after the last LUC meeting. FCC is receiving comments
and requesting feedback.

Discuss FCC Membership.
LUC has not made a decision about membership.
FCC is created by code and includes all community councils as members. Option is whether or not to send a delegate.

7.  Consider requesting amendment to 2026-0003 Amend AMC 21.05 and 21.15 to ease restrictions on agricultural uses and food
    production in Anchorage Bowl to include Chapter 9/Girdwood. P&Z Public Hearing is Jan 12 2026 (Edgington)
    https://www.muni.org/CityViewPortal/Planning/Status?planningId=18347
Item was LUC new business JAN. The current AO relates only to Anchorage/Eagle River and does not include T21C9 Girdwood code.
If Girdwood wants to be included, it can be done by requesting Assembly member submit “S” amendment to the current action or
engage to create a Girdwood-specific AO.




                                                                                         3

8.  Discuss appointment/Volunteer to serve on the Wildland Urban Interface-Community Action Team (WUI-CAT).

Motion:
GBOS moves to appoint Briana Sullivan as delegate to WUI-CAT, reporting to GBOS.
Motion by ME/2nd KO

Amendment:
Note that Briana will report to the Girdwood Fire Dept Board and to GBOS.
Amendment by KO/BS
roll call vote
Amendment carries 4-0

Amended Motion:
GBOS moves to appoint Briana Sullivan as delegate to WUI-CAT, reporting to Girdwood Fire Dept Board and to GBOS.
Motion carries by assent

9.  Agenda Item LUC 2510-07: LUC recommendation for GBOS letters regarding Solid Waste Services Fee increase (to be
    discussed at MOA GBOS Quarterly Meeting 1/26/26) (Wilbanks/Wingard).
Item was discussed at MOA GBOS meeting. MOA seemed receptive to the idea that the fee increase is over-impactful to those who are
using the dump to manage smaller amounts of trash more frequently. However, as this was an adopted AO, change would need to
come by similar mechanism with public process and will take some time to be adopted.

Motion:
GBOS moves to postpone this item to FEB GBOS meeting.
Motion by ME/2nd BS
Motion carries by Assent

Other topics discussed at the 4PM meeting were possibility of Sunday service and special recycling events for electronics, cardboard,
aluminum cans. These could come about more quickly than the change to fees.

NEW BUSINESS:
10. Agenda Item LUC 2601-04: LUC recommendation for GBOS action regarding Virgin Creek Avalanche Mitigation/Control
    Development Project Conditional Use Permit approval. (Tim Glassett, DOT&PF)
    Resolution of Support for zoning change, Conditional Use Permit
    https://www.muni.org/CityViewPortal/Planning/Status?planningId=18375.

11. GHEC current and upcoming vacancy: No volunteer response yet. GHEC may change operating rules to allow for smaller board.
    Deadline will be extended.

12. Safer Seward Highway proposal Home_DraftEA - Safer Seward Highway Safer Seward Highway
   Comment period extended to 2.27.26. Group discusses if there is community consensus to communicate to DOT on this item.

13. First Quarter Revisions. Likely GBOS will need to revise their 2026 budget. With change in assessments and assessed property,
    there is more space between GVSA budgets and tax cap than calculated during budget discussions in the fall.


REPORTS:
14. Reports (see packet)
    Supervisor reports:
Action Item Updates as assigned:
Request for GBOS/LUC Joint meeting: (0 of 2 required meetings held)
Request for GBOS/GFR Joint meeting (0 of 2 required held)
Request for Executive Session:
Other:
Adjourn 9:30PM
